name: macropad
title: Macropad for the thin module
orientation: A circuit board, made by a fab (JLCPCB), not printed. Seen from above: twelve keys in three columns and four rows; the module's USB-C on the top edge. Front: the module above the keys, display sockets below them. Rear: the module under the top row, parts facing down.

mount.rule: front: the module on top, beyond the keys, with display sockets; rear: the module under the top row of keys, on pin headers, the board no bigger than the keys
mount.label: Module

cols.rule: Columns of keys: three, the module's end columns being three key widths apart
cols.label: Columns

key_gpio.rule: The twelve GPIO the keys take, along the module's bottom row: not 0 and 1 (UART, for a split keyboard's halves), 2 and 3 (I2C display), 4 (spare) or the display's pins

module_gap.rule: Front: the module's bottom edge this far beyond the top row of keys' square

castle_out.rule: Front: each pin's pad reaches this far beyond the module's edge, for the solder fillet on a castellated half hole

strip.rule: Front: the strip below the keys for the display sockets and their labels

socket_in.rule: Front: each display socket's end pin this far in from the keys' side edge

label_gap.rule: Silkscreen labels this far from the pads they name

margin.rule: Front: board edge beyond the module's pads and the sockets, with room for an M2 hole in each corner

display_scl.rule: SPI display: SCL (clock), the module's display column

via_hole.rule: The router's vias: a 0.3 mm hole, JLCPCB's standard (no extra charge), with the ring it recommends

socket_turn.rule: The display sockets turned to lie along the board's bottom edge, pin 1 on the left (and their pins' names turned to run up the board)

label_char.rule: Silkscreen: a character's width, as a share of its height (tscircuit's font)

track.rule: Signal track width: well over JLCPCB's least on a cheap two-layer board

clearance.rule: Copper to copper, kept by the router
